reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) shows that trace interstitials in a single-phase RHEA cause phase segregation and matrix softening during 700°C aging, but it does not demonstrate grain boundary segregation, reduced grain boundary cohesion, or brittle intergranular fracture. The hypothesis's core claims about embrittlement and toughness loss are therefore unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Trace interstitials (O, N) segregate to grain boundaries under thermal and mechanical loading in single-phase HEAs.
This segregation reduces grain boundary cohesion and causes embrittlement.
The embrittlement leads to premature toughness loss and intergranular brittle fracture.
The mechanism is significant under high-temperature aging (e.g., 700°C) and long-term conditions.
Ultra-high-purity processing will prevent this segregation and the associated embrittlement.
